prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1492; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling through the intersection in Sugar Land, Texas, and reported that Driver 2 struck the side of the vehicle while turning left across the lane. Driver 1 stated that a wrist fracture resulted from bracing against the dashboard during the impact. The reporting officer observed that the reported injury is consistent with the kind and force of a collision of this type. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved. Passenger was seated in the front right position and was present in the vehicle at the time of the collision, as confirmed by statements from Driver 1 and Driver 2 at the scene. Damage to the left side of Driver 1's vehicle is consistent with the impact described by both parties. Scene photographs confirm the general placement of the vehicles and several of the reported damage points. A few older scratches were noted on the rear bumper and may predate this collision. No independent witnesses were located at the scene, and no third-party statements were obtained beyond those of the drivers and the passenger.
